A licence-safe digital savings wallet and lending platform for cooperatives — free to join, fully online, accounting-grade underneath.

Pitch deck · November 2026

The problem

Cooperative savers are underserved by the tools they’re given

Paper and office visits

Members queue to deposit, wait days to learn their balance, and apply for loans on forms. Trust erodes when records are slow or opaque.

Predatory digital credit

Loan apps fill the gap with hidden fees and abusive recovery — the reason the FCCPC tightened digital lending rules in 2025.

Licence mismatch

Off-the-shelf wallets come with transfer features a lending licence does not cover, creating regulatory risk for cooperatives.

30M+ Nigerians belong to cooperative societiesSource: Nairametrics, citing the cooperative federation (2023)

Licence-safe by design

A lending licence, not a payments licence — the product respects that

AllowedNot built, not exposed
Deposits into the member’s own walletMember-to-member transfers
Withdrawals to the member’s own, name-verified bank accountPayouts to third parties
Loan disbursement to own accountBills, airtime, cards, “send money”
Repayment from own savingsAny inter-bank transfer feature

Enforced in code: the payment adapter has no generic transfer function; payout accounts change only through staff verification.

Prompt Funds · Confidential5

Accounting-grade core

Every naira on screen ties to the books

  • Double-entry ledger — the database itself rejects unbalanced or edited entries
  • Idempotent money flows — webhook replays and double taps never double-post
  • Maker-checker on KYC, withdrawals, loan approval and disbursement
  • Live KPIs — liquidity cover, portfolio at risk, trial balance variance
  • Hash-chained audit trail for examiners and auditors

End-to-end tested: register → KYC → deposit → concurrent withdrawals → loan → repayment → interest; trial balance stays at ₦0.00.

Business model

Income from lending and permitted investments funds savings interest and operations

Illustrative year — 10,000 members₦m
Loan interest (₦480m avg. book @ 24%)115
Processing fees (1% of disbursements)10
Investment income (₦240m @ 15%)36
Total income161
Interest on savings (₦800m @ 8%)(64)
Expected loan losses (3%)(14)
Payment processing(30)
Technology & support(15)
Staff & operations(25)
Surplus before reserves13

Assumptions: average savings ₦80,000/member; 60% of savings lent; T-bill-type yield 15%. Illustrative only — rates are set by the board-approved policy.

Sensitivities that matter

  • Deposit fees are the largest variable cost — negotiate DVA caps, encourage fewer larger deposits
  • Every +1pt of savings rate costs ~₦8m a year at this scale
  • Each 1% of extra loan losses costs ~₦5m
  • Free registration stays a core principle
Prompt Funds · Confidential7

Why now

Regulation and rails have caught up

Clear lending rules

The FCCPC’s DEON Consumer Lending Regulations 2025 require registration and fair conduct — favouring transparent, member-owned lenders.

Dedicated virtual accounts

Payment partners now issue each customer a permanent account number, so transfers reconcile automatically.

Electronic identity

BVN/NIN verification APIs make remote onboarding fast and cheap, without office visits.

Data protection

Built for the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023: encrypted identity numbers, consent, access logs.

Serverless economics

Hosting starts at tens of dollars a month and scales with usage.

Web first

No app-store cost at launch; native apps when volume justifies.
